## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). ## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. - Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from

(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a

and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as

6	## Questions bloquantes
7	
8	**Q1. Which address does the trace trace, when Diagnostics already routed some?**
9	Only step 6 depends on it; steps 1 to 5 deliver the story without it.
10	
11	Today the trace resolves the name again (`net.DefaultResolver.LookupNetIP("ip4")`)
12	and takes `addrs[0]` (D144, hypothesis "the first IPv4 address"). The route stage
13	looked up the addresses of the Diagnostics resolution (`env.Resolve`, with the DNS
14	Server field when it is filled, at most 8). On a round-robin or CDN name, the
15	order changes from one resolution to the next. So the trace's `addrs[0]` is often
16	an address that Diagnostics did not look up, and the route is read again: AC1 holds
17	"per address" but the user still sees two readings, for two different addresses.
18	
19	- **(a) Strict, no change to the traced address.** Reuse only when `addrs[0]` is
20	  one of the addresses already looked up. Otherwise read the route once, for that
21	  address. No behaviour change beyond the story. Cost: on round-robin names reuse
22	  will often not happen.
23	- **(b) Prefer an address already looked up.** Among the IPv4 addresses the
24	  trace's own resolution returns *now*, take the first one Diagnostics looked
25	  up. If none, take `addrs[0]`. The traced address is still one the system resolver
26	  returns now (never an old one, never one from the custom DNS Server). It changes
27	  D144's "first IPv4 address" rule, and only when Diagnostics results exist.
28	- (c) Trace the Diagnostics address without resolving again. **Rejected**: the
29	  address may come from the DNS Server field, which the trace says it ignores
30	  (`traceUnusedNotice`), and it may be stale.
31	
32	**Recommendation: (b)**. It is what makes AC1 visible on real names, and the
33	traced address stays a current answer. If the answer is (a), skip step 6.
34	
35	## Hypothèses (prudent defaults, to confirm, not blocking)
36	
37	- **H1. "Trace again" reuses the same reading.** Inside the trace level, `enter`
38	  after a finished trace reuses the Diagnostics reading again, as long as the
39	  results it came from are still behind the trace level. The story says the reading
40	  is kept and discarded with the results ("no lifetime"), and "never two different
41	  values". To read again, the user runs `ctrl+r` on the results. Alternative
42	  rejected: re-reading on Trace again would let the trace row and the Diagnostics
43	  row show two values side by side.
44	- **H2. A container source reads its own route.** With `ctrl+o` on a container
45	  (story hypothesis), the route is read on every launch, as today. Going back to
46	  "this machine" reuses again.
47	- **H3. The Diagnostics `Local route` row is unchanged.** Same verdict, summary,
48	  reason, facts and explanation, and the same number of `env.Route` calls (one per
49	  address, at most 8). AC5.
50	- **H4. The `ERROR [netdiag/path] route` log line stays.** It is written for a
51	  reused error too: it describes the error behind the trace's rows. No new log.
52	- **H5. A route error seen by the trace itself is not a route reading.** A trace
53	  whose `nettrace` call fails with "no route" still sets the interface row to
54	  `no route` (`handleDoneError`, D20 proof). That is a new observation by the
55	  trace, not a second route reading. It can differ from a Diagnostics row that said
56	  routed a moment earlier. Kept as is.

58	## Constraints and non-functional requirements
59	
60	- **Rule 110.** The reading reaches the trace's `Cmd` as an immutable value
61	  (cloned slice) captured at launch, in `Update`. No `Cmd` reads `Model` or
62	  `PathModel`.
63	- **Rule 130 (one computation).** The trace's interface and gateway rows and the
64	  Diagnostics row come from the same `RouteHop` and the same `error`. The
65	  `no route` / `undetermined` classification stays `nettrace.IsNoRoute`, applied
66	  to that same error on both sides (`routeVerdict` and `newPathRoute`). AC4.
67	- **No global cache, no lifetime.** The reading is a field of the `CheckRoute`
68	  check inside `Model.results`. It is cleared by the same two assignments as the
69	  results (`StartRun`, `resetToForm`).
70	- **Cost.** At most 8 entries, cloned once per `openTrace`. No measurable load.
71	- **Exploitability.** No setting, no new log, no visible UI change except the

74	## Facts checked in the code (7b0b44d8)

76	- `netcheck.Check` exposes the route only as text facts (`Interface`,
77	  `Source address`, `Gateway`, `Route`, `No route`, `Route undetermined`). There is
78	  no structured `RouteHop` and no error value. Parsing the facts back is not

106	### Where the reading is kept
107	
108	| | Keep it | Reject it |
109	|---|---|---|

Snapshot on `PathModel`, decorate `engine.route` at launch** (recommended) | `openTrace` writes `pm.known` (the only writer). `launch` builds a per-run copy of the engine whose `route` answers from the snapshot first. `producePath`, `startPathRun` and their about 10 test call sites are unchanged. 127	
128	### Validity key: why a stale value cannot be reused
129	
130	A reading is reused only if all of these hold:
131	
132	1. **Same results.** The snapshot is built from `m.results` in `openTrace`, the
133	   only entry into the trace level. While the trace level is on screen, the results
134	   cannot change: the trace level takes the Diagnostics tab, and `ctrl+r` / `N` are
135	   results keys. `StartRun` (a new `Run Diagnostics`, `ctrl+r`) and `resetToForm`
136	   (`esc`, `N`) empty `m.results`. The next `openTrace` rebuilds the snapshot, and
137	   it is assigned on **every** `openTrace`, so it is never left over. An explicit
138	   run generation would add nothing: the snapshot never outlives an `openTrace`.

143	   results are kept.

145	   compared after `Unmap`. A new resolution that gives another address does not

148	   `pm.source.isHost()` (H2).

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

1	# DEVDESK-473 (P2-04): the local route is read once for Diagnostics and Trace Path
2	
3	Base: `main` at `7b0b44d8`. Package scope: `internal/netcheck`, `internal/ui/netdiag`.
4	Plan written by the architect; nothing here is implemented yet.
5	
6	## Questions bloquantes
7	
8	**Q1. Which address does the trace trace, when Diagnostics already routed some?**
9	Only step 6 depends on it; steps 1 to 5 deliver the story without it.
10	
11	Today the trace resolves the name again (`net.DefaultResolver.LookupNetIP("ip4")`)
12	and takes `addrs[0]` (D144, hypothesis "the first IPv4 address"). The route stage
13	looked up the addresses of the Diagnostics resolution (`env.Resolve`, with the DNS
14	Server field when it is filled, at most 8). On a round-robin or CDN name, the
15	order changes from one resolution to the next. So the trace's `addrs[0]` is often
16	an address that Diagnostics did not look up, and the route is read again: AC1 holds
17	"per address" but the user still sees two readings, for two different addresses.
18	
19	- **(a) Strict, no change to the traced address.** Reuse only when `addrs[0]` is
20	  one of the addresses already looked up. Otherwise read the route once, for that
21	  address. No behaviour change beyond the story. Cost: on round-robin names reuse
22	  will often not happen.
23	- **(b) Prefer an address already looked up.** Among the IPv4 addresses the
24	  trace's own resolution returns *now*, take the first one Diagnostics looked
25	  up. If none, take `addrs[0]`. The traced address is still one the system resolver
26	  returns now (never an old one, never one from the custom DNS Server). It changes
27	  D144's "first IPv4 address" rule, and only when Diagnostics results exist.
28	- (c) Trace the Diagnostics address without resolving again. **Rejected**: the
29	  address may come from the DNS Server field, which the trace says it ignores
30	  (`traceUnusedNotice`), and it may be stale.
31	
32	**Recommendation: (b)**. It is what makes AC1 visible on real names, and the
33	traced address stays a current answer. If the answer is (a), skip step 6.
34	
35	## Hypothèses (prudent defaults, to confirm, not blocking)
36	
37	- **H1. "Trace again" reuses the same reading.** Inside the trace level, `enter`
38	  after a finished trace reuses the Diagnostics reading again, as long as the
39	  results it came from are still behind the trace level. The story says the reading
40	  is kept and discarded with the results ("no lifetime"), and "never two different
41	  values". To read again, the user runs `ctrl+r` on the results. Alternative
42	  rejected: re-reading on Trace again would let the trace row and the Diagnostics
43	  row show two values side by side.
44	- **H2. A container source reads its own route.** With `ctrl+o` on a container
45	  (story hypothesis), the route is read on every launch, as today. Going back to
46	  "this machine" reuses again.
47	- **H3. The Diagnostics `Local route` row is unchanged.** Same verdict, summary,
48	  reason, facts and explanation, and the same number of `env.Route` calls (one per
49	  address, at most 8). AC5.
50	- **H4. The `ERROR [netdiag/path] route` log line stays.** It is written for a
51	  reused error too: it describes the error behind the trace's rows. No new log.
52	- **H5. A route error seen by the trace itself is not a route reading.** A trace
53	  whose `nettrace` call fails with "no route" still sets the interface row to
54	  `no route` (`handleDoneError`, D20 proof). That is a new observation by the
55	  trace, not a second route reading. It can differ from a Diagnostics row that said
56	  routed a moment earlier. Kept as is.
57	
58	## Constraints and non-functional requirements
59	
60	- **Rule 110.** The reading reaches the trace's `Cmd` as an immutable value
61	  (cloned slice) captured at launch, in `Update`. No `Cmd` reads `Model` or
62	  `PathModel`.
63	- **Rule 130 (one computation).** The trace's interface and gateway rows and the
64	  Diagnostics row come from the same `RouteHop` and the same `error`. The
65	  `no route` / `undetermined` classification stays `nettrace.IsNoRoute`, applied
66	  to that same error on both sides (`routeVerdict` and `newPathRoute`). AC4.
67	- **No global cache, no lifetime.** The reading is a field of the `CheckRoute`
68	  check inside `Model.results`. It is cleared by the same two assignments as the
69	  results (`StartRun`, `resetToForm`).
70	- **Cost.** At most 8 entries, cloned once per `openTrace`. No measurable load.
71	- **Exploitability.** No setting, no new log, no visible UI change except the
72	  consistency itself.
73	
74	## Facts checked in the code (7b0b44d8)
75	
76	- `netcheck.Check` exposes the route only as text facts (`Interface`,
77	  `Source address`, `Gateway`, `Route`, `No route`, `Route undetermined`). There is
78	  no structured `RouteHop` and no error value. Parsing the facts back is not
79	  possible without losing the error type (needed by `IsNoRoute`), so a structured
80	  field is needed.
81	- `Check` is already not comparable (`Facts`, `Phases` are slices), so adding a
82	  slice field breaks no `==`. `internal/mcp/netcheck_tools.go` maps `Check` to its
83	  own DTO (`checkOut`), so nothing new leaks into MCP.
84	- `runRoute` → `lookupRoutes` calls `env.Route` once per address
85	  (`targetAddresses`: a literal, or the `Address` facts of `CheckResolve`, as
86	  `net.IP`, often in 16-byte form for IPv4).
87	- Diagnostics runs through `runStageCmd`, which hardcodes
88	  `netcheck.SystemEnv(set)`: there is no seam for a counting `Env` in netdiag.
89	- The trace's address is a 4-byte `netip.Addr` (`ParseAddr` or `LookupNetIP("ip4")`).
90	  Matching needs `Unmap` on both sides (`addrFromIP` in `path_steps.go` already
91	  unmaps).
92	- `Model.openTrace` is the only entry into `StateTrace` (`tracePathFromRoute` with

133	   only entry into the trace level. While the trace level is on screen, the results
134	   cannot change: the trace level takes the Diagnostics tab, and `ctrl+r` / `N` are
135	   results keys. `StartRun` (a new `Run Diagnostics`, `ctrl+r`) and `resetToForm`
136	   (`esc`, `N`) empty `m.results`. The next `openTrace` rebuilds the snapshot, and
137	   it is assigned on **every** `openTrace`, so it is never left over. An explicit
138	   run generation would add nothing: the snapshot never outlives an `openTrace`.
139	2. **Same host.** `Model.resultsHost` is set by `StartRun` (the `Target.Host` the

145	   compared after `Unmap`. A new resolution that gives another address does not

  the target's traffic uses, with its source address, for example
